description: Fix Problem 1 (API key wrongly rejected) and lay the storage foundation for multi-provider support. Make API-key validation ROBUST so a network/transport failure inside the WebView is NEVER treated as an invalid key. Generalize Storage to persist a selected provider ('gemini'|'groq'|'openai') alongside its key, while keeping full backward compatibility with the existing single-key storage. Also generalize Storage.setPermission/getPermission to support 'mic', 'contacts', 'location', and 'accessibility'. This feature is foundational for FEAT-002 (routing) and FEAT-004 (permission UI). NOTE: This is the FIRST feature but there is NO runnable build/test in this sandbox (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, no network); establish the static-verification baseline instead of a green test run.
steps: Establish baseline: run `unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check js/storage.js js/app.js js/android-bridge.js js/gemini-chat.js js/gemini-voice.js js/functions.js` and confirm all pass BEFORE making changes. Run `node scripts/copy-web.js` and confirm it copies assets without error (pure Node, no network).

In js/storage.js: add provider persistence. Add KEYS entries for a provider marker and per-provider keys, e.g. KEYS.PROVIDER='mayra_provider' plus a helper that maps a provider id to its storage key (e.g. mayra_key_gemini / mayra_key_groq / mayra_key_openai) OR keep one active-key slot plus a provider marker. Add getProvider()/setProvider(p) (default 'gemini') and provider-aware setApiKey(key, provider?)/getApiKey(provider?)/hasApiKey(provider?)/clearApiKey(provider?). Keep the existing no-arg getApiKey()/setApiKey()/hasApiKey()/clearApiKey() behaviour working for callers that don't pass a provider (they should operate on the currently-selected provider). Preserve XOR obfuscation for all stored keys. BACKWARD COMPAT: if the legacy KEYS.API_KEY ('mayra_api_key') value exists and no new-format value is present, getApiKey() must still return it (treat it as the gemini key / active key) so users who already saved a key are not logged out.

In js/storage.js: generalize setPermission(name,status)/getPermission(name). Replace the hardcoded `name === 'mic' ? KEYS.PERM_MIC : KEYS.PERM_CONTACTS` ternary with a map from name -> storage key covering 'mic','contacts','location','accessibility' (add KEYS.PERM_LOCATION='mayra_perm_location' and KEYS.PERM_ACCESSIBILITY='mayra_perm_accessibility'). Unknown names must not throw; default to a namespaced key or return 'unknown'.
In js/storage.js: export any new public functions (getProvider, setProvider, and the provider-aware key helpers) in the returned object at the bottom of the IIFE.

In js/app.js validateAndSaveApiKey(context): REMOVE the hard format reject that blocks anything not starting with 'AIza' as the sole gate. Real Gemini keys do start with AIza but the true bug is that a network/transport failure currently reads as 'invalid'. Rework the flow so: (a) empty key -> warm error as today; (b) call a provider-aware validation that returns a THREE-way result: 'valid' | 'auth_error' | 'network_error' (never a bare boolean). Only 'auth_error' (HTTP 401/403 or a body indicating API_KEY_INVALID) should reject with a warm 'Yeh key kaam nahi kar rahi' style message. On 'network_error', SAVE the key anyway (Storage.setApiKey with the selected provider) and show a warm reassuring message: 'Network issue — key save kar li, baat karte waqt check ho jayegi'. On 'valid', save + success message as today. Keep the onboard->onboardNext() progression on success AND on network_error (key is saved either way).

In js/app.js: replace _testApiKey(key) with a provider-aware validator (e.g. _testApiKey(key, provider) returning one of 'valid'|'auth_error'|'network_error'). For gemini: POST to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent?key=KEY with a tiny body; res.ok OR status 400 => 'valid' (400 = reachable, key format acceptable), 401/403 => 'auth_error', any thrown/fetch error or other non-ok transport failure => 'network_error'. Structure it so FEAT-002 can add groq/openai branches (Bearer-auth endpoints). Never let a catch return 'invalid'; a catch is always 'network_error'.
Do NOT change gemini-chat.js / gemini-voice.js in this feature (multi-provider routing is FEAT-002). Keep MAYRA_SYSTEM_PROMPT untouched.
Verify: `unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check js/storage.js js/app.js`. Manually re-read the diff to confirm backward-compat path for legacy mayra_api_key and that no network catch maps to a rejection.
acceptance_criteria: `unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check js/storage.js js/app.js` passes with no syntax errors.

Storage exposes getProvider/setProvider and provider-aware key helpers, all listed in the returned public API object; a pre-existing legacy 'mayra_api_key' value is still returned by getApiKey() (backward compatible).
Storage.setPermission/getPermission handle 'mic','contacts','location','accessibility' without a hardcoded two-way ternary.

validateAndSaveApiKey never rejects a key solely because it does not start with 'AIza' and never rejects on a network/transport failure; on network failure it saves the key and shows the 'Network issue — key save kar li...' warm message; only a genuine 401/403/API_KEY_INVALID shows a 'key kaam nahi kar rahi' rejection.
_testApiKey returns a three-state result ('valid'|'auth_error'|'network_error'); a fetch throw always yields 'network_error', never a rejection.
Gemini voice and chat code paths are unchanged and still syntactically valid.
verification: node scripts/copy-web.js (confirms asset copy still works; pure Node, no network)
Re-read validateAndSaveApiKey + _testApiKey to confirm: catch => network_error (save+reassure), 401/403 => auth_error (reject), and no 'AIza' hard gate remains as the sole reject.
findings:
Implemented in commit 00d02bd (js/storage.js, js/app.js only). STORAGE: added KEYS.PROVIDER='mayra_provider', KEYS.PERM_LOCATION, KEYS.PERM_ACCESSIBILITY; PROVIDERS=['gemini','groq','openai'] with DEFAULT_PROVIDER='gemini'; per-provider key slots via _providerKeyName -> 'mayra_key_

'. getProvider/setProvider added and exported. setApiKey/getApiKey/hasApiKey/clearApiKey are now provider-aware with optional provider arg; no-arg calls operate on the active provider. BACKWARD COMPAT: getApiKey() falls back to legacy 'mayra_api_key' slot when active provider is gemini and no new-format value exists; clearApiKey() also clears the legacy slot for gemini so cleared keys don't resurface. XOR obfuscate/deobfuscate preserved for all stored keys. setPermission/getPermission now use a PERM_KEYS name->key map covering mic/contacts/location/accessibility; unknown names fall back to a namespaced 'mayra_perm_' key (no throw). APP: _testApiKey(key, provider) now returns three-state 'valid'|'auth_error'|'network_error' — gemini branch: res.ok||400 => valid, 401/403 => auth_error, other status or thrown fetch => network_error (a catch is ALWAYS network_error). Non-gemini providers currently return network_error (FEAT-002 will add real groq/openai Bearer validation). validateAndSaveApiKey: removed the 'AIza' hard-reject gate; on auth_error shows warm 'Yeh key kaam nahi kar rahi' rejection; on network_error SAVES the key under the selected provider and shows 'Network issue — key save kar li, baat karte waqt check ho jayegi'; on valid saves+success as before; onboardNext() fires on both success and network_error. No existing App exports removed. VERIFICATION (static, INTEGRATIONS_ONLY): `unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check js/storage.js js/app.js` passes; gemini-chat.js and gemini-voice.js unchanged and still pass node --check; `node scripts/copy-web.js` succeeds. www/ rebuilt for sanity but NOT committed (gitignored). No network/gradle/cap builds attempted (not available).
